slides.headline: She won a top Venice Film Festival prize in 2025. In 2026, she won another one - for a different film.
Anuparna Roy's "Lovers in the Blue Night" won the NETPAC Award for Best Asian Film at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival
slides.body: The Bengal-born filmmaker's second feature, set in Mumbai and following four people navigating love and belonging, premiered in Venice's Orizzonti section on September 11, 2026, with the award reported days later.

slides.headline: A year earlier, her debut film "Songs of Forgotten Trees" won Venice's Orizzonti Best Director award - making her the first Indian filmmaker to win that prize.
slides.body: Two different films, two consecutive years, two of Venice's most selective sections - a rare run for any filmmaker, let alone one still early in her career.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat benefits when its independent filmmakers keep winning at the world's oldest film festival, not just once.
slides.body: Roy's consecutive Venice wins signal that Indian independent cinema's international reputation isn't a one-off - it's becoming a pattern festivals now expect.
